mainTopic: Ranking the four death penalties: the רבנן's order (סקילה first) and רבי שמעון's order (שריפה first)
overview: The גמרא ranks the four deaths of בית דין: סקילה, שריפה, סייף and חנק. For the רבנן, סקילה is the most severe. A betrothed בת כהן gets סקילה, not שריפה, and they prove the rest of their order the same way. Each time, the גמרא first gives a reason based on who receives a death, such as the מגדף, the בת כהן, or the people of an עיר הנדחת. It then pushes back with אדרבה, pointing to another sinner, like one who strikes a parent. Each push-back is settled by a stronger proof: the Torah moving a case to a harsher death, a גזרה שוה on the word "אביה", or the rule that the מדיח is worse than the people he led astray. Then the גמרא explains רבי שמעון, who puts שריפה first, because he holds that even a betrothed בת כהן is moved from סקילה to שריפה. The proof that שריפה is more severe than סייף for רבי שמעון begins at the end of the amud and finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: The Rabbis: only a married בת כהן gets burning
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain their view: the special punishment of שריפה applies only to a married בת כהן who sinned, not to a betrothed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that a married בת כהן who sins is taken out to be burned, but a betrothed one is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to the question from just before this, about which death is more severe. They state that only a נשואה goes to שריפה, not an ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being clear about who gets שריפה sets up the proof that comes next. A betrothed בת כהן is treated like any other betrothed woman who sins, and she gets סקילה. The special שריפה rule covers only a married בת כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן hold (this is their opinion)
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
A married woman is taken out for burning,
phrases.notes: He means a married בת כהן who sinned with another man.

phrases.english: but not a betrothed one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's position in response to the discussion before this passage
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly: the שריפה rule covers only a נשואה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think any בת כהן who sins, even an ארוסה, gets שריפה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a married בת כהן gets שריפה; an ארוסה gets סקילה

steps.title: Proof that stoning is more severe
steps.stepSummary: The Torah takes the betrothed woman out of the regular rule and gives her סקילה, which shows that סקילה is the more severe death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah singled out the betrothed woman for stoning, we learn from this that stoning is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the רבנן's ranking. The Torah gave the betrothed woman סקילה, and that shows סקילה is the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married בת ישראל who sins gets חנק, but the Torah gives the ארוסה the stricter death of סקילה. According to the רבנן, even a betrothed בת כהן gets סקילה, not שריפה. If שריפה were harsher she would get it, since being betrothed and being a בת כהן both make her case stricter, so סקילה must be more severe than שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally, the Merciful One) took her out of the general rule

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, סקילה is more severe than שריפה. The proof is that the Torah singled out the ארוסה for סקילה.

phrases.english: And since the Merciful One took out the betrothed woman for stoning,
learn from this: stoning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּאַפְּקַהּ רַחֲמָנָא לַאֲרוּסָה בִּסְקִילָה שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition in step 1 to draw the ranking
steps.raayaObject: That סקילה is more severe than שריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah singled out the ארוסה for סקילה

steps.title: Stoning is more severe than the sword
steps.stepSummary: סקילה is ranked above סייף because the Torah gives it for מגדף and עבודה זרה, sins that attack the core of our faith.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stoning is more severe than the sword, since it is given to one who curses ה׳ and to one who worships idols. What makes those sins so severe? What we said before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new comparison: סקילה against סייף. It says סקילה is more severe because it is the punishment for the worst sins against faith.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is that the harshest sins get the harshest death. מגדף and עבודה זרה are treated as the most serious sins because they attack the foundations of belief, as the גמרא explained earlier. Since they get סקילה, סקילה ranks above סייף.

phrases.english: Stoning is more severe than the sword,
since it is given to one who curses ה׳
and to one who worships idols.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא explained that these sins strike at the very core of our faith.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְקִילָה חֲמוּרָה מִסַּיִיף שֶׁכֵּן נִיתְּנָה לִמְגַדֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from comparing סקילה with שריפה to comparing סקילה with סייף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סקילה is more severe than סייף because it is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה

steps.title: Challenge: maybe the sword is more severe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite: סייף is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת, whose property is also destroyed, so maybe סייף is the more severe death.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the sword is more severe, since it is given to the people of a city led astray into idol worship. What makes that so severe? Their property is destroyed too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 3 with אדרבה, which means "just the opposite." It points to the עיר הנדחת, where the punishment is סייף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of an עיר הנדחת also served idols, and on top of being killed, they lose all their property. That extra harshness suggests their sin is treated as even worse. If so, their death, סייף, should rank above סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people were led astray into idol worship

phrases.english: On the contrary: the sword is more severe,
since it is given to the people of a city led astray.
And what is the severity? That their property is destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the ranking given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that סקילה is more severe than סייף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The people of an עיר הנדחת get סייף and also lose their property, so their sin seems worse and סייף should rank higher

steps.title: The one who leads others astray is worse, and he is stoned
steps.stepSummary: The person who leads others astray is worse than the people he led astray. A ברייתא teaches that the inciters of an עיר הנדחת get סקילה, so סקילה stays the more severe death.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer: whose sin is greater, the one who leads others astray or the ones he led astray? Clearly the one who leads them astray. And a ברייתא teaches that the inciters of an עיר הנדחת are stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It compares the inciter with the people he misled and shows that the worse sinner, the inciter, gets סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the case of the עיר הנדחת itself, the inciter is the guiltier one. The ברייתא says inciters get סקילה, while the people of the city get סייף. So the worse sinner gets סקילה, which confirms that סקילה is more severe than סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means the weight or seriousness of the sin
One who leads others astray into idol worship
It is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The final ranking stays: סקילה is more severe than סייף. The proof is that the מדיחים, who are worse than the people they misled, get סקילה.
steps.confusionAlert: The people of the עיר הנדחת get סייף, but the people who led them astray get סקילה. Do not mix up the two groups.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ranking of the death penalties matters in practice. When a person is liable for two deaths, or when there is doubt about which death applies, the רבנן's ranking is used.

phrases.english: You can say: whose power is greater,
the power of the one who leads astray or the power of the one led astray?
phrases.notes: "Power" here means how serious the sin is.

phrases.english: You must say: the power of the one who leads astray.
And it is taught: those who lead astray the city that was led astray are executed by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 and keeps the ranking of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a worse sinner within the same case who receives סקילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the people of the עיר הנדחת get סייף and lose their property, סייף seemed to be the harsher death
steps.terutzMaskana: The inciters, who sinned more, get סקילה, so סקילה is more severe than סייף

steps.title: Stoning is more severe than strangulation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that סקילה is more severe than חנק, because סקילה is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה, sins that attack the core of our faith.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stoning is more severe than strangulation, because stoning is given to the blasphemer and to one who worships idols. And what makes those sins so severe? As we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pair in the ranking and claims that סקילה is more severe than חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It uses the same reasoning as before: סקילה is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה. Those sins attack the very foundation of our faith, so the death given for them must be the more severe one. The words "as we said" send us back to that earlier reason instead of repeating it.

keyTerms.meaning: Strangulation, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
As we said (pointing back to an earlier reason)
The severity, meaning what makes it so serious

phrases.english: Stoning is more severe than strangulation,
since it is given to the blasphemer
and to one who worships idols.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: "As we said" points back to the reason given earlier: these sins attack the core of our faith.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling סקילה over סייף, the גמרא opens the next comparison, סקילה versus חנק, using the same reason as step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סקילה is more severe than חנק because it is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Maybe strangulation is more severe, because of honoring parents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite: חנק is given to one who strikes his father or mother, and parents' honor is compared to the honor of הקב"ה, so maybe חנק is more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe, because it is given to one who strikes his father or mother. And what makes that sin so severe? Because the honor of parents is compared to the honor of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ranking from step 6 and suggests that חנק might be the more severe death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses the same kind of reasoning as step 6: look at which sin gets the death. חנק is given to מכה אביו ואמו, and the Torah compares honoring parents to honoring הקב"ה. So the sin punished with חנק also touches on honor owed to ה׳, and חנק could be just as serious, or even more serious.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; it is the opposite
One who strikes his father or mother (and wounds them)
Was compared; the Torah puts the two side by side

phrases.english: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe,
since it is given to one who strikes his father or his mother.
And what is the severity?
Because their honor is compared to the honor of the Omnipresent.
phrases.notes: "Their honor" means the honor of the parents. "The Omnipresent" is a name for ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly reverses the ranking stated in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that סקילה is more severe than חנק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we rank a death by the sin it punishes, חנק punishes striking parents, whose honor is compared to ה׳'s honor. That is a reason to rank חנק at least as high as סקילה.

steps.title: The Torah moves the betrothed woman from strangulation up to stoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that סקילה is more severe from the Torah itself: a betrothed בת ישראל who sins is taken out of the general rule of חנק and given סקילה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah took a betrothed Jewish woman out of the category of a married Jewish woman, changing her death from strangulation to stoning, learn from this that stoning is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7 with a proof from the Torah, not from reasoning about which sin is worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married בת ישראל who sins gets חנק, but the Torah singles out the betrothed one and gives her סקילה. When the Torah takes a case out of its group and changes its death, it is making it stricter. So סקילה must be more severe than חנק, and that settles the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Took it out, singled it out from the general rule
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: The final proof that סקילה is above חנק does not come from comparing sins. It comes from the Torah moving the betrothed woman from חנק up to סקילה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two women. Here we are talking about a בת ישראל, an ordinary Jewish woman, not a בת כהן. The married one gets חנק and the betrothed one gets סקילה.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One took out a betrothed Jewish woman
from the category of a married Jewish woman,
from strangulation to stoning,
learn from it: stoning is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and restores the ranking from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the structure of the פסוק (the Torah removes a case from its general group and changes its death).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since honoring parents is compared to honoring ה׳‎, חנק might be the more severe death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah's move of the betrothed woman from חנק to סקילה proves that סקילה is more severe.

steps.title: Burning is more severe than the sword
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new comparison: שריפה is more severe than סייף, because it is given to a בת כהן who sinned, and she shames her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning is more severe than the sword, because it is given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery. And what makes her sin so severe? Because she profanes her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pair in the ranking and says that שריפה is more severe than סייף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the גמרא ranks the death by the sin it punishes. A בת כהן who sins does not only harm herself, she also brings shame on her father the כהן. That extra harm is why her death, שריפה, is ranked above סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning, one of the four death penalties

phrases.english: Burning is more severe than the sword,
since it is given to a priest's daughter who committed adultery.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי חוּמְרָא? שֶׁכֵּן מְחַלֶּלֶת אֶת אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: And what is the severity? Because she profanes her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling סקילה over חנק, the גמרא opens a new comparison between שריפה and סייף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שריפה is more severe than סייף because it is given to a בת כהן who sinned and shamed her father.

steps.title: Maybe the sword is more severe than burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: סייף should be more severe than שריפה, because סייף is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת, who also lose all their property.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: the sword is more severe, because it is given to the people of a city led into idol worship. What makes that so severe? Their property is destroyed too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 9 that שריפה is worse than סייף, arguing the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said שריפה is worse because a בת כהן shames her father. The challenge says סייף is worse, because the people of an עיר הנדחת receive it, and their punishment is so harsh that even their property is destroyed. A penalty given to a crime with such a heavy extra punishment looks like the more severe one.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
A city whose people were led into עבודה זרה
And what is the severity? (what makes it so severe)

phrases.english: On the contrary: the sword is more severe,
since it is given to the people of a city led into idol worship.
And what is the severity there?
That their property is destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the reasoning of step 9 by giving a competing reason for the opposite ranking.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שריפה is more severe than סייף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סייף is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת, whose crime is so grave that even their property is destroyed. That suggests סייף is the harsher penalty.

steps.title: The word "her father" links burning to stoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a גזרה שוה: the word "אביה" appears with סקילה and with שריפה. Just as סקילה is more severe than סייף, so is שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Her father" is written about stoning, and "her father" is written about burning. Just as with stoning, which is more severe than the sword, so too with burning: it is more severe than the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a Torah-based link (גזרה שוה) instead of more logical reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word "אביה" both for the betrothed נערה who gets סקילה and for the בת כהן who gets שריפה. We already know סקילה is more severe than סייף, so the shared word teaches that שריפה is also more severe than סייף. This ends the back-and-forth of logical arguments with a source from the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both
Just as... so too... (the comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: שריפה is more severe than סייף. This is proven from the shared word "אביה," which ties it to סקילה.

phrases.english: "Her father" is stated regarding stoning,
and "her father" is stated regarding burning.
Just as with "her father" stated regarding stoning,
stoning is more severe than the sword,
so too with "her father" stated regarding burning,
burning is more severe than the sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by bringing a source from the פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural proof through a גזרה שוה that overrides the competing logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the harshness of עיר הנדחת, סייף might be more severe than שריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared word "אביה" links שריפה to סקילה, so like סקילה, שריפה is more severe than סייף.

steps.title: Burning is more severe than strangulation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new comparison: שריפה is more severe than חנק, because it is given to a בת כהן who sinned, for the reason already stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning is more severe than strangulation, because it is given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery. What makes that so severe? As we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to compare שריפה with חנק and gives a reason why שריפה is worse. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reason from step 9 is reused here: a בת כהן who sins shames her father, which makes her sin especially serious. Since she gets שריפה, שריפה looks more severe than חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן's daughter who committed adultery
As we said (pointing back to an earlier reason)

phrases.english: Burning is more severe than strangulation,
since it is given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 9: she shames her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling שריפה versus סייף, the גמרא turns to a new pair: שריפה versus חנק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שריפה is more severe than חנק because it is given to a בת כהן who sinned and shamed her father.

steps.title: Maybe strangulation is more severe because of parents' honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: חנק might be more severe, because it is given to one who strikes his father or mother, and parents' honor is compared to the honor of הקב"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe, because it is given to one who strikes his father or mother. What makes that so severe? Their honor is compared to the honor of the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 12 that שריפה is worse than חנק, and argues the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One who strikes a parent gets חנק. The Torah treats the honor of parents like the honor of הקב"ה, so striking a parent is a very grave sin. That suggests חנק, the penalty for it, may be the more severe death.

keyTerms.meaning: One who strikes and wounds his father or mother
Was compared (the Torah set two things side by side)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same argument the גמרא used in step 7 against סקילה. Now it is aimed at שריפה. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe,
since it is given to one who strikes his father or his mother.
And what is the severity there?
That their honor is compared to the honor of the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the reasoning of step 12, using the same parents' honor argument that was used in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שריפה is more severe than חנק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנק is given for striking a parent, and parents' honor is compared to the honor of הקב"ה. That makes the sin very grave, so its penalty, חנק, may be the harsher death.

steps.title: The Torah moved the married בת כהן from strangulation to burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 13. The Torah took a married בת כהן out of the normal rule for a married woman and changed her punishment from חנק to שריפה. This shows שריפה is more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah took the married daughter of a כהן out of the general group of married Jewish women, and changed her punishment from strangulation to burning, we learn from this that burning is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of whether חנק might be more severe than שריפה. It proves from the Torah's own wording that שריפה is the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal married woman who sins with another man gets חנק. The Torah singled out the married בת כהן and gave her שריפה instead. The Torah would only make a special change to make her punishment harsher, because she shames her father, so שריפה must be the more severe death.

keyTerms.meaning: Since the Torah (literally, the Merciful One) took it out

steps.whatToRemember: שריפה is more severe than חנק. We know this because the Torah moved the married בת כהן from חנק up to שריפה.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One took out
the married daughter of a priest
from the general group of a married Jewish woman
changing her from strangulation to burning,
learn from it: burning is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 that חנק might be more severe than שריפה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from how the Torah built the punishments: a special change for one case shows which punishment is harsher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חנק might be more severe because it is the punishment for striking a parent, and a parent's honor is compared to הקב"ה's honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah moved the married בת כהן from חנק to שריפה, so שריפה is more severe.

steps.title: The sword is more severe than strangulation
steps.stepSummary: A new comparison begins: סייף is more severe than חנק, because it is the punishment for the people of an עיר הנדחת, who also lose all their property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sword is more severe than strangulation, because it is the punishment for the people of an idol-worshipping city. And what makes it more severe? Their property is destroyed as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new comparison between סייף and חנק. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will push back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from who receives סייף: the people of an עיר הנדחת. Their punishment is extra harsh because their property is destroyed too, not only their lives. So סייף seems to be the harsher death.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people were led into idol worship

phrases.english: The sword is more severe than strangulation,
since it is given to the people of an idol-worshipping city.
And what is the severity?
That their property is destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The שריפה and חנק comparison is finished, so the גמרא moves on to compare סייף and חנק, using the same עיר הנדחת reasoning from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סייף is more severe than חנק because it is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת, who also lose their property.

steps.title: Maybe strangulation is more severe, because of striking a parent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: חנק may be more severe, because it is the punishment for striking one's father or mother, and a parent's honor is compared to הקב"ה's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe, because it is the punishment for one who strikes his father or mother. And what makes it more severe? That parents' honor is compared to the honor of הקב"ה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim it just made and argues the opposite: חנק might be the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge points to who receives חנק. One who strikes a parent gets חנק, and the Torah compares honoring parents to honoring הקב"ה. So that sin seems very serious, which would make חנק a harsh punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: One who strikes his father or mother

phrases.english: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe,
since it is given to one who strikes his father or mother.
And what is the severity?
That it is compared, etc.
phrases.notes: The word כו׳ means "and so on." It points back to step 13: a parent's honor is compared to the honor of הקב"ה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15's claim that סייף is more severe than חנק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 15 that סייף is more severe than חנק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנק is given for striking a parent, and a parent's honor is compared to הקב"ה's honor, so it may be the harsher punishment.

steps.title: Denying הקב"ה Himself is still worse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: even so, the people of an עיר הנדחת deny the very foundation, הקב"ה Himself. That is worse than striking a parent, so סייף stays more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, one who stretches out his hand against the very foundation is worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps its ruling that סייף is more severe than חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Striking a parent only hurts an honor that is compared to הקב"ה's honor. The idol worshippers of an עיר הנדחת attack the honor of הקב"ה Himself directly. So their sin is worse, and their punishment, סייף, is the harsher one.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rejects the foundation of the faith, meaning הקב"ה
Is greater, weighs more (here, is the worse sin)

steps.whatToRemember: Ranking so far: סייף is more severe than חנק, because attacking הקב"ה directly (עיר הנדחת) is worse than attacking an honor that is only compared to His (striking a parent).
steps.confusionAlert: Here עדיף does not mean "better." It means this sin weighs more, so it is the worse sin.

phrases.english: Even so,
one who stretches out his hand against the foundation is worse.
phrases.notes: "The foundation" means הקב"ה Himself. These are the idol worshippers of the עיר הנדחת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, פּוֹשֵׁט יָדוֹ בָּעִיקָּר עָדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16's challenge and confirms step 15's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing the sins: a direct attack on הקב"ה outweighs an honor that is only compared to His.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Striking a parent is so serious that חנק might be more severe than סייף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Denying הקב"ה Himself is worse, so סייף is more severe than חנק.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: burning is more severe than stoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון's view in the משנה. It explains that שריפה is more severe than סקילה because שריפה is the punishment for a בת כהן who commits adultery, and she brings shame on her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says, etc. Burning is more severe than stoning, because it is the punishment for a כהן's daughter who committed adultery. What makes it so severe? She profanes her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section on רבי שמעון's order of the deaths. It gives his first reason: שריפה is worse than סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses the type of sinner who gets שריפה. A בת כהן who sins does more than sin herself: she brings disgrace on her father, the כהן. So the punishment given to her is treated as a heavier one.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא in the משנה who holds that burning is the most severe death
She profanes (brings disgrace on) her father

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה, where רבי שמעון gives his own order of the deaths, with burning first.

phrases.english: Burning is more severe than stoning,
since it is given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery.
And what is the severity?
Because she profanes her father.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳. שְׂרֵיפָה חֲמוּרָה מִסְּקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבנן's ranking in steps 1-17 to רבי שמעון's ranking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, שריפה is more severe than סקילה, because it is given to a בת כהן who profanes her father.

steps.title: Challenge: stoning is given for blasphemy and idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe סקילה is more severe, because it is the punishment for the מגדף and for one who serves עבודה זרה. These sinners attack the very foundation of faith, הקב"ה Himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: stoning is more severe, because it is the punishment for the blasphemer and for the idol worshipper. What makes it so severe? He attacks the very foundation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 18. It argues that סקילה should be the most severe death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 judged severity by the sinner: the בת כהן shames her father. The challenge uses the same method and finds worse sinners who get סקילה. Attacking הקב"ה is worse than shaming a father, so by that logic סקילה wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'stretches out his hand against the foundation', meaning he attacks הקב"ה Himself

phrases.english: On the contrary: stoning is more severe,
since it is given to the blasphemer
and to one who worships idols.
And what is the severity?
Because he stretches out his hand against the foundation.
phrases.notes: The 'foundation' here is הקב"ה Himself, the root of all faith.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that שריפה is more severe than סקילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If severity is judged by the sinner, the sinners punished with סקילה (מגדף, עבודה זרה) attack הקב"ה, which is worse than shaming a father. So סקילה should be more severe.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's own view about the betrothed בת כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון holds a בת כהן gets שריפה whether she is ארוסה or נשואה. A normal betrothed woman gets סקילה, but the Torah moved the betrothed בת כהן from סקילה to שריפה. This shows that שריפה is more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, because he says: whether she is betrothed or married, a כהן's daughter goes out to burning. Since the Torah took the betrothed כהן's daughter out of the rule for a regular betrothed woman, changing her punishment from stoning to burning, learn from it that burning is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 19 with a proof from the Torah itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothed woman who sins normally gets סקילה. רבי שמעון holds that a betrothed בת כהן gets שריפה instead. The Torah treats her sin as worse because she is a בת כהן, so it would not lighten her punishment. The new punishment, שריפה, must therefore be heavier than סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (a view he holds elsewhere)
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before נישואין
The Torah (the Merciful One) took it out of the general rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 14. There the proof used a married בת כהן, moved from חנק to שריפה. Here it uses a betrothed בת כהן, moved from סקילה to שריפה. This proof works only because רבי שמעון holds that a betrothed בת כהן also gets שריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי שמעון's ranking rests on a Torah exception, not only on reasoning about how bad the sinner is. So the challenge in step 19 cannot overturn it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, for he says:
whether betrothed or married,
she goes out to burning.
phrases.notes: He is talking about a בת כהן who committed adultery.

phrases.english: And since the Merciful One took out
the betrothed daughter of a כהן
from the general category of a betrothed daughter of a Yisrael
from stoning to burning,
learn from it: burning is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and backs up the claim of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a Torah-based proof that follows the speaker's own known view, instead of weighing which sinner is worse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since סקילה is given for attacking הקב"ה, it seemed to be the most severe death.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Torah moved the betrothed בת כהן from סקילה to שריפה, שריפה is more severe according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, a betrothed בת כהן gets שריפה instead of סקילה. That switch proves שריפה is worse than סקילה.

steps.title: Burning is also more severe than strangulation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues רבי שמעון's order: שריפה is more severe than חנק too. The reason is the same as before: it is given to a בת כהן who sinned and shamed her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning is more severe than strangulation, because it is the punishment for a כהן's daughter who committed adultery. What makes it so severe? As we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next comparison in רבי שמעון's list. It ranks שריפה above חנק, using the reason from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the reasoning. The same point, that the בת כהן profanes her father, now shows that שריפה is worse than חנק as well.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said (pointing back to an earlier reason)

phrases.english: Burning is more severe than strangulation,
since it is given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 18: she profanes her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next comparison in רבי שמעון's order, after the שריפה versus סקילה comparison was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, שריפה is more severe than חנק, for the same reason: the בת כהן profanes her father.

steps.title: Maybe strangulation is more severe, since it is for striking a parent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that שריפה is worse than חנק. It argues that חנק might be worse, because it is the punishment for one who strikes his father or mother, and honoring parents is compared to honoring הקב"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: חנק is more severe, because it is given to one who strikes his father or mother. And what makes that so severe? Their honor is compared to the honor of הקב"ה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 21. Maybe חנק, not שריפה, is the more severe death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 judged שריפה by the serious sinner who gets it, the בת כהן. Here the גמרא uses the same kind of reasoning for חנק: it is given to someone who strikes a parent, and the Torah links a parent's honor to הקב"ה's honor. So the sinner who gets חנק might be the worse one.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary. It opens a challenge that argues the opposite.
Strangulation, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
One who strikes his father or mother so that it leaves a wound
Was compared. The Torah puts two things side by side so that they share a law.

phrases.english: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe,
since it is given to one who strikes his father or his mother.
And what is the severity?
Because their honor is compared to the honor of the Omnipresent.
phrases.notes: The Torah describes honoring parents in a way that matches honoring הקב"ה, so striking a parent is very serious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 21's claim that שריפה is more severe than חנק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 21 that שריפה is more severe than חנק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a punishment is judged by the sinner who receives it, then חנק goes to one who strikes a parent. Parents' honor is compared to הקב"ה's honor, so חנק may be more severe.

steps.title: The Torah moved the married בת כהן from strangulation to burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a married בת ישראל who commits adultery gets חנק, but the Torah singled out a married בת כהן and gave her שריפה instead. This shows that שריפה is more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah took the married בת כהן out of the group of married women and moved her from חנק to שריפה, we learn that שריפה is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 22 with the same kind of proof it used in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing how bad different sinners are can go either way. A direct move in the Torah is much stronger. The same sin, adultery by a married woman, normally gets חנק. When the sinner is a בת כהן, the Torah makes her punishment harsher and gives her שריפה, so שריפה must be the worse death.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah took it out, meaning the Torah singled out a case
A Jewish woman who is not from a כהן's family
Learn from this, or conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of thumb: when the Torah moves a case from one death to another to make it harsher, the death it moves to is the more severe one.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One took out the married daughter of a priest
from the category of a married Jewish woman,
from strangulation to burning,
conclude from it: burning is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 using the same kind of proof as step 20, this time for a married woman instead of a betrothed one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the Torah moving a case from one punishment to another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חנק might be more severe, since it is given to one who strikes a parent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah moved the married בת כהן from חנק up to שריפה, so שריפה is more severe.

steps.title: Burning is also more severe than the sword
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next pair in רבי שמעון's order: שריפה is more severe than סייף. The reason is the same as before. It is given to a בת כהן who sinned, and she shames her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: שריפה is more severe than סייף, because it is given to a בת כהן who committed adultery. And what makes that so severe? As we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to compare שריפה with סייף, using the reason it already gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has shown that שריפה is worse than סקילה and worse than חנק. Now it compares שריפה with סייף. "As we said" points back to step 18: her sin also shames her father.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by the sword (beheading), one of the four death penalties
As we said. It points back to a reason given earlier.

phrases.english: Burning is more severe than the sword,
since it is given to a priest's daughter who committed adultery.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 18: she shames her father by her sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing שריפה against חנק, the גמרא now compares שריפה with סייף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי שמעון's order, שריפה is more severe than סייף because it is given to a בת כהן who sinned and shamed her father.

steps.title: Maybe the sword is more severe, since the עיר הנדחת also loses its property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 24. Maybe סייף is more severe, because it is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת, and they also lose all their property.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: סייף is more severe, because it is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת. And what makes that so severe? Their property is also destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 24 by arguing that סייף might be the more severe death. The answer will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same argument the גמרא used in steps 4, 10 and 15: on top of dying, the people of an עיר הנדחת lose their property. A punishment that also takes away everything they own may count as harsher.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people were led to serve עבודה זרה. Its people are killed and its property is burned.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this reason up with step 17. There, the עיר הנדחת was severe because its people denied הקב"ה. Here, the reason is that they also lose their property.

phrases.english: On the contrary: the sword is more severe,
since it is given to the people of an idolatrous city.
And what is the severity? Because their property is destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 24's claim that שריפה is more severe than סייף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that שריפה is more severe than סייף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סייף is given to the people of an עיר הנדחת, who also lose all their property. That extra loss may make סייף the harsher punishment.

steps.title: Who is worse: the one who leads astray or the one who is led astray?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer the challenge from step 25 by asking which sin is greater: the sin of the מדיח or the sin of the נידח.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should say: Whose sin is greater, the sin of the one who leads others astray, or the sin of the one who is led astray?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to answer the challenge that סייף might be worse than שריפה. It asks a question that compares the person who leads others astray with the people who follow him. This sets up the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of an עיר הנדחת get סייף, but they are only the followers who were led astray. The person who led them astray, the מדיח, gets סקילה, so סקילה is harsher than סייף. Step 20 already showed that for רבי שמעון שריפה is harsher than סקילה, so שריפה must also be harsher than סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: "You should say": a way of introducing the answer to a challenge
Literally "strength"; here it means the weight or seriousness of a sin
The one who leads others to worship idols
The one who was led astray to worship idols

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a question, but it is not a new challenge. It is the start of the גמרא's answer. The obvious answer, that the מדיח is worse, comes in the very next line.

phrases.english: You should say: But which severity is greater,
the severity of the one who leads astray, or the severity of the one led astray?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the קשיא of step 25 by comparing the מדיח with the people of the עיר הנדחת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing punishments: the followers' punishment (סייף) cannot be harsher than the leader's punishment (סקילה), because the leader's sin is greater.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the people of an עיר הנדחת get סייף and also lose all their property, maybe סייף is the most severe death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The followers are less guilty than the one who led them astray, so סייף is not the harshest. This supports רבי שמעון's order that שריפה is more severe than סייף. The conclusion is made explicit in the next line.
